findings.reason: the second arm must be restated as `run-queued`, otherwise the gate contradicts the behaviour it is meant to preserve.
findings.text: §8's done-when requires a queued request with no failure to yield the present `queued-awaiting-session` row, but that kind is built at reckon/crew/obligations.py:2075-2077 only when `row["session_refusal"]` is set, and a failure-free queued request is built by `_queued_item` as `QUEUED_RUN_DUTY_KIND` = `run-queued` (obligations.py:191, :944), so the arm asserts a row the tree never builds and an implementer would either write a test that cannot pass on correct code or change the plain queued row's kind, which is the confusion §8 exists to remove

findings.reason: the write paths must include reckon/crew/obligation_snapshot.py, or the branch must move into one helper both producers call, and the done-when must assert both producers.
findings.text: §8's write paths are reckon/crew/obligations.py and the new test only, but the queued branch is built twice: the derivation at obligations.py:2075 and the published slice at reckon/crew/obligation_snapshot.py:1457-1467, which builds the same `queued-awaiting-session` row through `module._live_item` for the payload a reader is handed; a new kind added only to the derivation leaves the slice on the old kind, and the done-when's obligations-only test passes while the two producers disagree

findings.reason: one sentence naming the node-contract refusal as the only family that moves keeps the follower row's kind and its test intact.
findings.text: §8's deliverable gives a row of its own kind to every queued request whose pointer carries an admission refusal, which is broader than the node-contract refusal the section evidences: the same `queued-awaiting-session` kind is today produced for a follower or other session-subject refusal (reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py:286-304) and for a refusal quoting the command that clears it (:309-311), and tests/test_a_session_side_refusal_reaches_the_session.py:150 pins that kind for a session-side refusal — the plan does not say which refusal family moves, so an implementer may move all of them and break a pinned behaviour the section was not about

findings.reason: either §2's shared signature must carry the resolved lane or backend settings, or §7's write paths must gain dispatch.py and dispatch_plan.py; without one of those the queue-time check has no production caller, which is the only reason the section exists.
findings.text: §7 says the shared function §2 extracts also runs the context-fit estimate against the request's resolved lane, but the estimate reads the window from a resolved backend (_context_fit_verdict and resolution.backend_settings, reckon/crew/routing.py:3560-3600) while §2 fixes the function's arguments as the node, repository, execution capability, locked decisions and budget ceiling with no lane or backend settings; the call sites that hold the resolved lane are queue_requests (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:293, which resolves the lane from backend_name or config) and plan_dispatch (reckon/crew/dispatch_plan.py:834), and neither file is in §7's write paths (dispatch_admission.py, dispatch_batch.py, the new test), so the signature change reaches callers outside the node's exclusive scope

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `_context_file_inputs` is at reckon/crew/routing.py:3262, and reckon/crew/obligations.py:2077 and `QUEUED_AWAITING_SESSION_DUTY_KIND` at :181 all resolve.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §8's done-when asserts that a queued request with no failure yields the present `queued-awaiting-session` row, but that kind is emitted only when a session refusal is present; a failure-free request is built as `run-queued`.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — both sections measure a test file inside the repository and their gate logs follow the run-directory convention; neither names a scratchpad or node-local temporary path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new test names describe the property measured (test_a_batch_entry_fits_its_window_when_queued.py, test_a_refused_request_names_its_refusal.py) with no plan labels, stage names or tracker numbers.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §8 changes the kind of an obligation row in one of the two producers that build it, so the published slice keeps the old kind; and §7's context-fit check needs a resolved lane that §2's shared signature does not carry, with the supplying call sites outside §7's write paths.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §7 carries one check (context fit at queue time) and §8 one obligation kind; each has one measurable test.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §7's "it runs after §2 and §6" is stated in prose and is enforceable as a run wait through the multiple `--after` option (reckon/crew_dispatch_commands.py:1171), the mechanism the plan's earlier §6 answer recorded; §8 takes no dependency and writes one module.
